_readme: SS-605. Routes whose PROSE states how many corrections the page carries.
This file exists because the rule used to be gated on the thing it was checking.
SS-605 read data-correction-count off the page and skipped any page that did not
have it -- so deleting the attribute deleted the check, silently, and the prose
claim went unverified. B7 in docs/validator-blind-spots.md.
Declaring the route here instead means the expectation survives the attribute.
Remove data-correction-count from the page and SS-605 now errors, because this
file still says the page states a count. Same shape as data/og-overrides.json:
the declaration lives outside the page so the page cannot silence it.
Add a route here when its copy states a correction count in words. Remove it only
when that sentence is gone from the page -- not when the attribute is.

routes.statedIn: The 'Updated August 2026' intro callout: 'Five are marked so far: ...'
routes.reason: The article enumerates its own corrections in prose. That sentence is a derived value and it was already wrong once -- it said four when a fifth was added on 2026-08-21.
